scope: Verified locators and lexical/object rules against ISO 32000-2:2020(E), sponsored edition including Errata Collection 3: 7.2, 7.3 and Tables 1-5, including numeric errata #300/#327 and identifier erratum #379; also checked rectangle representation in 7.9.5. Cross-reference/trailer locators 7.5.4/7.5.5 and Table 15 were checked against the same text, but document-level implementation behavior was not audited. Known core implementation discrepancies remain open; verified locators do not certify all consumers.

verification_source.edition: ISO 32000-2:2020(E), sponsored edition including Errata Collection 3
verification_source.errata: The supplied supplements #300/#327 affect numeric syntax and #379 affects indirect identifiers; none of the supplied supplements changes clause 7.4.

errata: EC3 #300 and #327, 7.3.3 numeric examples and grammar diagrams

rules.rule: Whitespace separates tokens, comments act as whitespace, syntax is case-sensitive, and braces are extra delimiters in Type 4 calculator functions.
rules.implementation: Whitespace and comments agree; global brace delimiting prevents braces in ordinary literal names.
rules.fixtures: Existing syntax tests cover separators/comments; minimal discrepancy: /A{B becomes name A with two bytes left, rather than name A{B.

rules.rule: Objects distinguish booleans, integer and real forms; signed decimal forms allow leading zeros, while radix and exponent spellings are excluded.
rules.implementation: Agrees for the inspected forms, including integer 00987 and real 009.87; native numeric representation is bounded.
rules.fixtures: Existing numeric syntax tests agree; the EC3 leading-zero examples were also checked directly.

rules.rule: Strings are byte sequences; literal escapes, octal truncation, continuations and EOL normalization apply, while odd hex strings receive a final zero nibble.
rules.implementation: Agrees in the inspected parser branches.

rules.rule: Literal names expand #xx escapes, exclude decoded NUL, preserve byte identity and permit an empty name.
rules.implementation: Agrees for escaping/NUL/empty names; brace classification remains a separate contextual discrepancy.
rules.fixtures: Existing name tests agree for covered byte/escape cases.

rules.rule: Arrays preserve heterogeneous element order; dictionary keys are direct names and duplicate keys are invalid.
rules.implementation: Agrees in parser construction; duplicate recovery is explicitly reported.
rules.fixtures: Existing array/dictionary and duplicate-key tests agree.

rules.rule: A null dictionary value has the same interpretation as an absent entry.
rules.implementation: Raw source dictionaries retain null values; semantic consumers must apply absence/default behavior. Codec consumers are corrected; other consumers were not audited.
rules.fixtures: Codec null-parameter vectors cover its consumers; raw dictionary retention is not claimed to prove semantic handling everywhere.

rules.rule: Streams are indirect, have a direct dictionary and encoded Length, and begin after LF or CRLF; Filter and DecodeParms describe ordered decoding.
rules.implementation: The core parser handles the direct dictionary; complete stream framing belongs to pagura-document and was not audited here.
rules.fixtures: Stream-filter pairing is covered in codec; no new verdict on complete document framing.

rules.rule: References identify object and generation; undefined objects resolve to null, and identifiers exclude plus signs and leading zeros except generation zero itself.
rules.implementation: The parser silently accepts 01 0 R and 1 00 R as references, contrary to EC3 #379.
rules.fixtures: Existing reference tests lack these invalid-identifier cases; both minimal reproducers were confirmed.

rules.rule: Classic xref entries have a fixed 20-byte form and a trailer locates the last section and identifies root/size information.
rules.implementation: Primary clause/table locators and basic rules checked; the cross-reference/trailer implementation is outside this lexical/object audit.
rules.fixtures: Existing document tests remain evidence, but no new xref/trailer implementation-conformance verdict is asserted.

requirements.gaps: EC3 #379 identifier restrictions and contextual brace handling remain implementation discrepancies. Null semantics, complete stream framing, cross-reference tables and trailers require consumer-level review.

rules.rule: A rectangle contains four numeric coordinates of opposite corners; neither a particular corner order nor positive width/height is required.
rules.implementation: Agrees: from_array accepts four numbers and from_corners normalizes either orientation, including degenerate rectangles.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: pagura-core rect tests and classic/normalized-media-box.

requirements.gaps: No broad geometric conformance claim beyond this rectangle representation rule.
